title: Chapter 120 — Performance Management and The Hard Conversations
intro: Standards enforced fairly, the improvement protocol, and the respectful exit.

sections.title: Standards Must Be Enforced
sections.content:
Setting high standards means nothing if you do not enforce them. Inconsistent enforcement is worse than no standards at all — because it teaches the team that standards are optional.

Enforcement does not mean punishment. It means accountability. 'We agreed your closing goal was 35%. You are at 22%. Let us figure out why and build a plan to get there.'

That is a coaching conversation, not a disciplinary one. But it is direct and honest. Avoiding it does not help anyone.

sections.title: The Improvement Protocol
sections.content:
When someone is underperforming, follow a structured process. Identify the gap. Observe and diagnose the root cause. Build a specific improvement plan with clear actions and a timeline. Coach consistently through the plan. Measure progress at defined checkpoints.

The key word is specific. 'Sell more' is not a plan. 'Complete a full product demonstration with every customer this week and log the outcome in CRM' is a plan.

sections.title: The Respectful Exit
sections.content:
Sometimes it does not work out. Despite coaching, support, and a clear plan, the person cannot or will not meet the standard.

When that happens, the exit should be handled with respect and professionalism. No surprises — they should have seen this coming through the improvement process. No hostility — this is a business decision, not a personal one.

How you exit someone says as much about your leadership as how you hire them. The rest of the team is watching.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating performance management, ask:

Are standards being enforced consistently — or selectively?
Is there a structured improvement protocol — or just verbal warnings?
Are hard conversations happening when needed — or being avoided?
When exits happen, are they handled with respect and professionalism?
